places.name: Gravensteen Castle
places.ai_summary: Gravensteen Castle, also known as the Castle of the Counts, is a medieval fortress in Ghent. It features a museum, dungeons, and panoramic views from the ramparts.
places.place_tip: Climb to the top for stunning views of Ghent.

places.name: St. Bavo’s Cathedral (Adoration of the Mystic Lamb)
places.ai_summary: St. Bavo’s Cathedral is a Gothic masterpiece in Ghent, housing the famous altarpiece 'Adoration of the Mystic Lamb' by the Van Eyck brothers. It is a spiritual and artistic treasure.
places.place_tip: Don’t miss the audio guide for the altarpiece.

attribution.author: Mylius
attribution.description: Ghent, Belgium: Sint-Baafskathedraal (Saint Bavo Cathedral) as seen from the top of the opposing bell tower

places.name: Graslei and Korenlei Canals
places.ai_summary: The Graslei and Korenlei are two picturesque streets along the river in Ghent, known for their stunning medieval architecture and vibrant atmosphere.
places.place_tip: Take a boat tour for a different perspective.

places.name: Belfry of Ghent
places.ai_summary: The Belfry of Ghent is a medieval bell tower and a UNESCO World Heritage site. It offers panoramic views of the city from its tower.
places.place_tip: Visit during sunset for a magical view.

attribution.title: Belfry of Ghent (DSCF0247,DSCF0249)
attribution.author: Trougnouf (Benoit Brummer)
attribution.description: This place is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, listed as Belfries of Belgium and France.

places.name: St. Nicholas’ Church
places.ai_summary: St. Nicholas’ Church is a beautiful Gothic church in the heart of Ghent, known for its impressive architecture and stunning stained glass windows.
places.place_tip: Attend a concert for a unique experience.

attribution.title: Sint-Niklaaskerk and the belfry of Ghent (DSCF0229)
attribution.author: Trougnouf (Benoit Brummer)
attribution.description: This place is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, listed as Belfries of Belgium and France.

places.name: Patershol Medieval Quarter
places.ai_summary: Patershol is a charming medieval neighborhood in Ghent, featuring narrow cobblestone streets, historic buildings, and a variety of restaurants and shops.
places.place_tip: Try the local cuisine at a Patershol restaurant.

places.name: Museum of Fine Arts (MSK)
places.ai_summary: The Museum of Fine Arts (MSK) in Ghent is an art museum featuring a rich collection of Flemish and Belgian paintings, sculptures, and decorative arts.

opening_hours.notes: Free admission on Saturdays after 1 PM.

places.place_tip: Check out the museum shop for unique art gifts.

attribution.title: Museum voor schone kunsten gent

attribution.description: Front view of the Museum of Fine Arts in Ghent Belgium

places.name: SMAK Contemporary Art Museum
places.ai_summary: SMAK is the Municipal Museum of Contemporary Art in Ghent, showcasing an extensive collection of modern and contemporary artworks.

opening_hours.notes: Free admission on Thursdays after 5 PM.

places.place_tip: Don’t miss the temporary exhibitions.

attribution.title: Smakedificio
attribution.author: Cristina Pastor
attribution.description: Façade of the SMAK (City Museum for Contemporary Art) museum in Gent

places.name: St. Peter’s Abbey & Gardens
places.ai_summary: St. Peter’s Abbey is a former Benedictine monastery in Ghent, featuring beautiful gardens, a church, and a brewery.

opening_hours.notes: Garden access may be restricted in winter.

places.place_tip: Join a brewery tour for a unique experience.

attribution.title: Gent Blandijn 005
attribution.author: Demeester
attribution.description: De Sint-Pietersabdij aan de oever van de Schelde in Gent, gezien vanaf de Muinkaai.

places.name: Vrijdagmarkt Square
places.ai_summary: Vrijdagmarkt is a historic square in Ghent, known for its vibrant market, stunning architecture, and the iconic statue of Jacob van Artevelde.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited during the market hours.

places.place_tip: Try the local delicacies at the market stalls.

attribution.title: The Friday Square - Ghent, Belgium - panoramio
attribution.author: Sergey Ashmarin

places.name: Graffiti Street
places.ai_summary: Graffiti Street is a famous alley in Ghent, known for its ever-changing street art and graffiti. It’s a vibrant and creative spot in the city.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited during the day for photography.

places.place_tip: Bring a camera to capture the street art.

places.name: Design Museum Ghent
places.ai_summary: Design Museum Ghent is a museum dedicated to design in all its forms, featuring a diverse collection of applied arts, design objects, and contemporary art.
places.place_tip: Explore the museum shop for unique design items.

attribution.title: Museum voor schone kunsten gent
attribution.author: marie-julie
attribution.description: Front view of the Museum of Fine Arts in Ghent Belgium

places.name: Kouter Flower Market
places.ai_summary: Kouter Flower Market is a famous flower market in Ghent, held every Sunday. It’s a colorful and fragrant experience in the city’s heart.
places.place_tip: Arrive early for the best selection of flowers.

places.name: Ghent City Museum (STAM)
places.ai_summary: Ghent City Museum (STAM) is the city museum of Ghent, showcasing the history, art, and culture of the city through interactive exhibits and collections.
places.place_tip: Don’t miss the panoramic view from the museum tower.

places.name: Old Fish Market
places.ai_summary: The Old Fish Market in Ghent is a historic market hall, now home to various food stalls and restaurants. It’s a great place to taste local delicacies.

opening_hours.notes: Check individual stalls for specific hours.

places.place_tip: Try the local seafood dishes.

places.name: Gravensteen Rooftop View
places.ai_summary: The rooftop view of Gravensteen Castle offers a stunning panoramic view of Ghent, including the city’s medieval architecture and the River Lys.
places.place_tip: Visit at sunset for a breathtaking view.

places.name: Gentse Feesten Festival (Seasonal)
places.ai_summary: Gentse Feesten is an annual cultural festival in Ghent, featuring a wide range of performances, concerts, and events throughout the city.

opening_hours.notes: Check the festival program for details.

places.place_tip: Book accommodations and tickets in advance.

places.name: Canal Boat Tour
places.ai_summary: A Canal Boat Tour in Ghent offers a unique perspective of the city’s historic architecture and picturesque canals.

opening_hours.notes: Check the schedule for departure times.

places.place_tip: Bring a light jacket, it can be windy on the water.

places.name: Citadel Park
places.ai_summary: Citadel Park is a public park in Ghent, featuring walking paths, a pond, and the Citadel of Ghent. It’s a great place for a leisurely stroll or a picnic.
places.place_tip: Visit the Citadel for a dose of history.

places.name: Sint-Michiels Bridge Viewpoint
places.ai_summary: The Sint-Michiels Bridge Viewpoint offers a stunning panoramic view of Ghent’s medieval architecture, including the Saint Michael’s Church and the Graslei.
places.place_tip: Visit at sunrise for a magical view.
